The tastings helped introduce consumers to the diversity of the grape — from elegant, restrained Zinfandels with bright acidity to powerful, fruit-rich versions from old vineyards. Once and Future is the new label of wine icon Joel Peterson. • 2024 Once and Future Zinfandel Teldeschi Vineyard The legendary Joel Peterson, founder of Ravenswood Winery, is hard at work with this new label producing wines from some of the same iconic vineyards he made at Ravenswood. This bottle from Dry Creek Valley’s Teldeschi Vineyard opens with aromas of cherries, chocolate, stone fruit preserves, lavender and blackberries. Medium to full-bodied, it explodes with copious juicy fruits and spicy accents, knit by soft tannins with a long savory finish. Three Wines sources Zin from ancient vineyards in Contra Costa County. • 2018 Three Wine Company Zinfandel Live Oak Vineyard Three Wine Company specializes in wines from ancient (1885) often overlooked vineyards in Contra Costa County. This wine has Petite Sirah and Carignan added to the Zinfandel for complexity. It has aromas of flowers, sweet briery fruit, raspberries, licorice and cherries that emerge from this attractive, dark ruby-colored, medium bodied The Annual Zinfandel tasting was held at Fort Mason Zinfandel. With good sweetness as well as pure fruit, this wellmade stylish effort has eight years of bottle age and is refined and ready to drink. • 2024 Terra Amata Old Vine Zinfandel This wine from the Dry Creek Valley was new to me. It bursts from the glass with a captivating bouquet in which aromas of roses, cherries and wild berries mingle with nuances of spice and forest floor. Full-bodied, satiny, and expansive on the palate, it’s multidimensional, succulent, and juicy, with amazing intensity concluding with a long, perfumed finish. • 2023 Tres Sabores Por Que No? This everything but the kitchen sink blend features Zinfandel, Petite Sirah, Cabernet and Petite Verdot. It is a delicious ebullient party wine bursting with blueberry, plum, and cherry flavors. Medium bodied with great acid and tons of finesse it is refreshing and balanced with a clean finish. Fire up the BBQ and throw on the burgers. • 2022 Limerick Lane Zinfandel Banfield Vineyard From an ancient Russian River Valley vineyard planted in 1880 Limerick Lane has created a wine that boasts a dense purple color in addition to a gorgeous nose of leather, spice box, plums and blueberries. It is big and full in the mouth but exquisitely balanced. It is built to last for a decade in the cellar. • 2024 We Know Jack Zinfandel Rockpile The rather new Rockpile AVA has never disappointed me. It is showing itself to be the perfect terroir for Zinfandel. The We Know Jack wine is packed with loads of cassis and blueberry fruit along with pepper, spice, earth and leather. This is a deep, rich, full-bodied, spicy Zinfandel that is immensely satisfying. • 2024 Williams Selyem Zinfandel Papera Vineyard Williams Selyem is so famous for their world-class Pinot Noirs that their Zinfandels can get overlooked. This Russian River Zin shows a sweet nose of black fruits intermixed with smoke, dried herbs and subtle wood. Rich and explosively ripe with a multilayered texture, this exceptional wine can be drunk now or cellared for 5-6 years. • 2023 Guyomar Oblate Hailing from Paso Robles this wine is a blend of Zinfandel, Petite Sirah and Grenache. This is a big muscular gorgeous wine with a dense purple color and lovely levels of blueberry, and raspberry fruit. The wine is an opulent fleshy, classic Zinfandel. Its purity, texture and full-bodied richness are impressive. Drink it over the next five or six years. • 2022 Hendry “Block 28” Zinfandel The always reliable George Hendry crafts his Zins with a high percentage of new French oak which gives a charming exotic vanilla-tinged nose. The Block 28 is a compelling wine graced with expressive dark fruit, flowers, cocoa, and licorice. It shows gorgeous finesse, plenty of mid-palate richness and terrific overall balance. Sweet floral notes and succulent black cherries wrap around the finish. • 2023 Wilson “Snake Patch” Zinfandel The Wilson family of wineries are expert at crafting beautiful fruit-forward Zinfandels. This wine offers copious quantities of Provencal garrigue-influenced plum and blueberry fruit intermixed with earth, pepper and baking spice. This medium to full-bodied luscious heady Zinfandel is delicious and would be a great partner to BBQ’d ribs. • 2023 Robert Biale Zinfandel Pagani Ranch Biale Winery has long been a master at hand crafting powerful yet elegant Zinfandels. This wine shows a sweet nose of black fruits intermixed with smoke, dried herbs and subtle wood. Rich and explosively ripe with a multilayered texture, this exceptional wine can be drunk now or cellared for 4-5 years. • 2022 Harney Lane Zinfandel Lizzy James Vineyard Lodi is the home to this wine whose dense purple color is followed by aromas of sweet, jammy black fruits, licorice, pepper, and minerals. Deep, rich and full-bodied, this impressively extracted wine exhibits moderate tannins, adequate acidity, and an impressive finish. A great example of Lodi’s fruit-forward style of Zinfandel. • 2021 David Clinton Zinfandel Teldeschi Vineyard The David Clinton Zins are a perpetual favorite of mine at ZAP. The wine reveals ripe raspberry and cherry fruit with notions of spice and leather in its fragrant, expressive bouquet. Medium-bodied, with nicely integrated wood, and no hard edges, it will drink well for 5 to 7 years. Rockpile AVA is the source for this Dashe Zinfandel. • 2023 Dashe Zinfandel Rocky Ridge Vineyard This single vineyard Zin from the excellent Rockpile AVA has a splash of Petite Sirah and Carignan added to round out the wine. The wine gets a good dash of new French oak giving it a charming nose of blueberry, anise, black pepper, cassis, herbs de Provence and vanilla. It is a fleshy, juicy wine loaded with ripe dark red fruit, flower, mint and spices. It possesses excellent mid-palate fleshiness in an open accessible personality with great aging potential. • 2022 Perlegos Duetto Inspired by the wines of Sicily the Duetto is a 50/50 blend of Zinfandel and Nero d’Avola. Medium garnet-purple colored, the Duetto gives up very spicy notes of pepper, anise, and cloves over prunes and blackberries with hints of currant jelly and soil. It is full, soft and juicy in the mouth with a chewy frame, great acidity and peppery finish. Very different and fun. • 2021 Grgich Hills Miljenko’s Old Vine Zinfandel This is the estate’s premier Zinfandel from old vines near Calistoga. It is graced with expressive dark red fruit, flowers, mint, and licorice. It shows gorgeous finesse, plenty of mid-palate richness and terrific overall balance. Sweet floral notes and succulent black cherries round out the finish.

Although their numbers have grown significantly, wild herds and those in private and public reserves remain genetically isolated. What nature is unable to do naturally at this point, due to decreased genetic diversity and population sizes, Oakland Zoo can provide support through a captive breeding program. “Witnessing the bison roam in their historical lands adds a profound beauty and significance that is difficult to capture without experiencing Montana firsthand. We bring these moments back to our Bay Area community, followers, and the Bay Area indigenous diaspora, truly bringing our mission to life and igniting our passion to continue advocating for this cause,” said Oakland Zoo CEO Nik Dehejia. Guests visiting the Zoo, whether from the Bay Area or around the world, can become part of the story by learning about the program that links culture, history, and animal care. Oakland is just a chapter in the ongoing story of these bison’s future, as the program reconnects them with their sacred land in Montana. “With the birth of its 50th calf, the Oakland Zoo is helping bring home far more than buffalo to the Blackfeet Nation. Together, we are restoring threads that were once severed—between people and place, culture and identity, memory and future—showing what becomes possible when restoration is rooted in relationship,” said Cristina Mormorunni, Executive Director of Indigenous LED. As bison return to Montana – more than 40 since the partnership began – the program continues to advance. Oakland Zoo Animal Care staff work daily in the 13-acre California Trail habitat to deliver gold-standard care to the herd, including enrichment, training, and herd management. The Zoo’s Veterinary Care staff provide medical services, including annual examinations, vaccinations, and hoof care. “We provide the necessary care to ensure a healthy herd of bison until their release, but the Blackfeet care for their soul. We feel privileged and proud to have participated in this journey, with four successful releases. We consider it a great honor to have the trust of our Blackfeet partners. It is an opportunity to be involved in a program that restores a part of a culture that was once taken away,” said Angela Gibson, Zoological Manager at Oakland Zoo. This ongoing effort underscores Oakland Zoo’s commitment and opens a clear path to deepen collaboration with the Indigenous LED organization. The Zoo will partner with tribes to advance conservation action, strengthen the systems that support long-term restoration, and develop the next generation of changemakers — positioning the program as a catalyst for ecosystem recovery and cultural revitalization.
